record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Study the stability of fronts in dissipative equations using renormalization-group methods.

evidence.quote: The major open problems listed in [BK2] are the study of stability of fronts in dissipative equations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional dissipative semilinear parabolic equation of the form
    u_t = u_{xx} + F(u),  x ∈ ℝ, t ≥ 0,
(or a system thereof, including the real and complex Ginzburg–Landau equation u_t = u_{xx} + u − |u|^{2}u) that admits a traveling front solution u(x,t) = φ(x − ct) joining two equilibria, with profile φ satisfying φ(−∞) = a, φ(+∞) = b and speed c ∈ ℝ.

A front φ is said to be (asymptotically) stable if there exists a neighborhood 𝒩 of φ in a suitable Banach space of perturbations such that for every initial datum u₀ ∈ φ + 𝒩 the solution u(x,t) of the equation satisfies, for some asymptotic phase x∞,
    ‖u(·, t) − φ(· − ct − x∞)‖ → 0  as t → ∞,
with quantitative decay rates.

Problem. Develop a renormalization-group framework for the long-time asymptotics of solutions to such dissipative equations near a traveling front, in which the rescaling u_n(x,t) = L^{α} u(L^{n} x, L^{2n} t) is iterated and a fixed point of the renormalization map is identified with the front profile. Using this framework, prove asymptotic stability (with optimal decay rates) of the relevant traveling fronts — including marginally stable / critical "pulled" fronts whose decay is governed by linear spreading and which lie outside the scope of maximum-principle techniques — for general classes of dissipative parabolic equations and systems (in particular complex Ginzburg–Landau type equations).
artifact.status_search_result: Renormalization-group methods have been successfully applied to prove stability of fronts in several dissipative equations: Bricmont–Kupiainen (1994) proved stability of moving fronts in the Ginzburg–Landau equation, and Bricmont–Kupiainen–Lin extended the RG method to general nonlinear parabolic PDEs. Gallay and others later established local stability of critical (pulled) fronts. Thus the program has yielded substantial results in concrete cases, but a complete and unified theory of front stability via RG for general dissipative systems remains an ongoing area of research, so the overall program is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Stability of moving fronts in the Ginzburg-Landau equation
status_evidence.snippet: Bricmont and Kupiainen use renormalization group ideas to prove stability of moving fronts in the Ginzburg-Landau equation, including complex perturbations beyond the maximum principle.
status_evidence.claim: RG-based stability of fronts has been established for the Ginzburg–Landau equation.

status_evidence.title: Renormalization group and asymptotics of solutions of nonlinear parabolic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Bricmont, Kupiainen and Lin present a general RG method for long time asymptotics of nonlinear parabolic PDEs, applicable to fronts and systems.
status_evidence.claim: A general RG framework for parabolic PDE asymptotics, including fronts, has been developed.

status_evidence.title: Local stability of critical fronts in nonlinear parabolic PDEs
status_evidence.snippet: Gallay proves local stability of critical (pulled) fronts using RG-type analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Critical front stability has been treated via renormalization-group-type methods.
